text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"The drop in baseline QA accuracy after ~40 appended items is caused by cross‑fact interference that exceeds the effective working‑set capacity, and can be alleviated by periodically consolidating the stored context into a compressed summary—as shown in the consolidation papers—thereby raising the interference threshold and preserving recall performance.","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["e8af7ee8","085f93d4","45562236"],"tags":["interference","consolidation","capacity"]},{"statement":"Integrating a virtual‑memory paging mechanism (e.g., MemGPT) to move older context out of the active window and back in on demand will emulate the benefits of a rewrite‑based memory without performing explicit rewrites, which explains the observed superiority of rewrite over naive append and suggests a hybrid approach for the planned rewrite‑vs‑append ablation studies.","confidence":0.62,"support_ids":["800e430c","d421fc37","e8af7ee8"],"tags":["virtual_memory","rewrite","ablation"]}]}
